title: Carboplatin · 21-day breast schedule

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with DNA copying and repair. This can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, and kidney function determines how the medicine is cleared.
agents.watch: Contact the oncology emergency service immediately for fever or shaking chills, sudden illness, bleeding, new breathlessness, chest pain or severe allergy. Report reduced urine, hearing changes and new numbness promptly. Do not wait for the next visit.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Infusion allergy, particularly with repeat platinum exposure
Fertility effects and harm to an unborn baby

purpose: Aim to slow or shrink metastatic breast cancer and help symptoms, balancing possible benefit, side effects and treatment burden.
schedule_summary: Carboplatin is infused on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team selects the dose using the prescribed AUC and kidney function. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated; there is no fixed breast course length.

sources.title: Current Irish product information · safety supplement

phases_title: The phases and how they connect
phases_note: These are the medicines in this exact schedule. Dose holds, missed tablets and omitted visits need instructions from your treating team.
timeline_note: This is a relative reference, not an appointment calendar. Treatment days can change after clinical review. Symptom bands do not predict when an effect will occur.
safety_note: A day without treatment is not automatically a safe day. Use the emergency contact when needed; do not move or restart doses yourself.
teachback: Which treatment days and doses are prescribed, which blood tests must happen first, how do you take the support medicines, and which symptoms need urgent help?
consent_support: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant. Carboplatin may affect periods and fertility, sometimes permanently. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss reliable contraception and contact the team immediately if pregnancy is possible. The linked Irish SmPC advises effective contraception for women during treatment and at least 6 months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least 3 months afterwards. Confirm the actual product/local advice and any longer requirement from other medicines. Discuss low blood counts and sepsis, bleeding, nausea/vomiting, fatigue, kidney, hearing and nerve effects, and infusion allergy. Benefit is uncertain and alternatives depend on your cancer and priorities. Carboplatin for metastatic breast cancer is an off-label use under this Irish NCCP protocol. The treating team must explain this, obtain informed consent and follow local Drugs and Therapeutics Committee approval requirements.
urgent_extra: Contact the oncology emergency service immediately for fever or shaking chills, sudden illness, bleeding, new breathlessness, chest pain or severe allergy. Report reduced urine, hearing changes and new numbness promptly. Do not wait for the next visit.

support.title: Preventing sickness
support.text: Take the prescribed anti-sickness medicines before treatment and on the following days, even if you feel well. Follow your own prescription and contact the team if nausea or vomiting is not controlled.

support.title: Blood counts
support.text: Keep blood tests and use the emergency contact for fever, chills or bleeding. Preventive growth-factor injections depend on individual risk.

support.title: Kidneys and other medicines
support.text: Tell the team about every medicine or supplement, especially treatments that affect kidneys, hearing or bleeding. Follow individual drinking advice.

support.title: Steroid and rescue plan
support.text: The anti-sickness plan may affect sleep, glucose and bowel symptoms. Confirm the exact doses and last day of each medicine; contact the team if symptoms persist.

questions.q: Is everyone given the same dose?
questions.a: No. The consultant selects an AUC target within the source range and the team uses verified kidney function and previous effects to calculate the dose. Do not calculate or change it yourself.

questions.q: How many cycles will I have?
questions.a: The breast source continues until cancer progression or unacceptable toxicity. The team agrees response reviews and continuation; the fixed course of a particular trial or another cancer type does not set your course.
These two carboplatin monotherapy protocols do not mandate routine heart scans. Tests are arranged when symptoms, other medicines or your individual risks make them appropriate.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: In the TNT study of advanced triple-negative or inherited BRCA1/2-associated breast cancer, carboplatin was active, but did not outperform docetaxel in the full study population. The inherited BRCA1/2 subgroup responded more often to carboplatin. These findings help inform a treatment discussion; they do not predict an individual result.
evidence.interpretation: The team considers previous treatment, cancer features, health and your priorities. A response in a trial cannot guarantee benefit for an individual.
evidence.limitations: Evidence and alternatives are discussed for your exact setting. Trial survival averages are not an individual prediction.

items.title: Breast treatment context
items.text: Advanced breast cancer. This patient suite describes the breast setting; the source protocol also has other tumour indications with their own clinical context.

items.title: Schedule and duration
items.text: Carboplatin is infused on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team selects the dose using the prescribed AUC and kidney function. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated; there is no fixed breast course length.

items.title: How treatment is given
items.text: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes after blood and symptom review and prescribed anti-sickness medicines. The complete appointment takes longer. A cannula or existing line may be used; a port is not automatically required.

items.title: Off-label breast indication
items.text: Carboplatin for metastatic breast cancer is an off-label use under this Irish NCCP protocol. The treating team must explain this, obtain informed consent and follow local Drugs and Therapeutics Committee approval requirements.

chapters.title: Checks before and during treatment
chapters.intro: Every dose depends on the reviewed treatment plan and results.

items.title: Blood and symptom checks
items.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle. The team confirms the kidney-function method, current AUC and previous dose changes. Report numbness, hearing changes, infection and bleeding. Additional tests follow symptoms and the individual plan.

items.title: Heart and response checks
items.text: Kidney dosing, hearing and nerve review are central. Scans follow the consultant plan; no universal heart-scan schedule is specified.

items.title: Fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant. Carboplatin may affect periods and fertility, sometimes permanently. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss reliable contraception and contact the team immediately if pregnancy is possible. The linked Irish SmPC advises effective contraception for women during treatment and at least 6 months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least 3 months afterwards. Confirm the actual product/local advice and any longer requirement from other medicines. Discuss low blood counts and sepsis, bleeding, nausea/vomiting, fatigue, kidney, hearing and nerve effects, and infusion allergy. Benefit is uncertain and alternatives depend on your cancer and priorities.

sections.title: Visits and tests
sections.text: One infusion visit per 21-day cycle plus pre-cycle blood tests and clinical review. Additional tests depend on symptoms and the individual plan.

sections.title: Treatment preparation
sections.text: Your team chooses venous access. A port is optional, requires a separate insertion procedure and later removal; it is not removed after every infusion.

sections.title: At home
sections.text: Allow time for blood review, preparation, anti-sickness treatment, the infusion and observation. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.

sections.title: Contacts / follow-up
sections.text: Keep emergency contacts, medicine lists and the next appointment plan. Report line redness, swelling, leakage, pain or fever promptly.
